summary: Ling Ji is a sinologist who completed her PhD at the National University of Singapore (attested 2014) under doctoral supervisor Yuet-Keung Lo.

Linnart Mäll (1938–2010) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Tartu (~1957–1962) and under Bidia Dandaron (~1967–1972), later holding a post at the University of Tartu (~1966–2010).
Linus Klemp works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He held a PhD post at the University of Copenhagen in 2025 and is attested there as a PhD Fellow in 2026.
Lionel Burton Burrows (1883–1970) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology who studied at St. Paul's School in Darjeeling and at Elphinstone College.

Lionel David Barnett (1871–1960) studied Indology and linguistics at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell and at Liverpool. He held posts at the British Museum (1899–1936, 1948), University College London (1906–1917), and SOAS (1917–1948).
Lionel James Trotter (1827–1912) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Charterhouse School (~1841–1845) and Merton College (~1845–1847).

Lionel Obadia (b. 1968), a religious and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his PhD at the University of Lille (-1997). He held posts at INALCO (1996), KU Leuven (2000), EPHE (2002), Lille III (attested 2002), and Lyon 2 (attested 2010–2014).

Liqian Liu (1910–2008) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1944–1949), the State Council's translation administration department, and the Ethnic Publishing House (~1956–1979).

Lisa Grumbach works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She was affiliated with Stanford University (attested 1996) and served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Lisa N. Owen specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her M.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Texas at Austin under Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lise Menn (b. 1941) is a linguist who studied at Swarthmore College (~1958–1962), Brandeis University (~1962–1964), and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1971–1976). She served on the faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder (1986–2007).
Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008) under supervisor Jens Braarvig in 2003.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) studied Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies at Peking University (~1951–1956) under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian. He served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1956–2014).

Liz Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (1985–1992), where she lectured from 1991 to 1992, and became Associate Professor of Religion at Miami University in 1992.
Liza Zigmund-Cerbu (1924–1965) was a religious studies scholar who studied in 1947 at both the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Aganina (1926–2000) was an Indologist and linguist. She worked in the redaction of Sovetskoe vostokovedenie (1954–1958) and as a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1958).

Ljudmila Aleksandrovna Mervart (1888–1965), an Indologist and linguist, studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1910). She held posts at Far Eastern Federal University, Kunstkamera, the Institute of Ethnology and Anthropology, Military Institute of Foreign Languages, and Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies.

Lloyd W. Pflueger works in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He completed a doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Choedak studied Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2012–2013). He worked at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (2013–2018) and became a lecturer at CIHTS in 2018.

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (until 1959), and completed his doctorate at the University of Munich by 1974.
